s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent skin lesion with possible metastasis
salient_findings: Recurrent skin lesion on the dorsum of the right thumb
key_facts: 56-year-old man
Four-year history of skin lesion on the right thumb
Partial amputation of the thumb in December 2016
Lesion reappeared in August 2017
No significant medical history
No medications
1.8 × 1.3 cm lesion on the dorsum of the right thumb stump
Lesion is mobile over deep structures
No palpable lymphadenopathy
Metastatic workup included CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis and a bone scan
Enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node presumed to represent metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive skin cancer with high metastatic potential

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Highly aggressive skin cancer with rapid growth and metastasis

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common skin cancer with possible metastasis, although less likely

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Locally aggressive skin cancer with possible metastasis

raw.rationale: The lesion's recurrence after partial amputation and the presence of an enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node suggest an aggressive skin cancer, which is more typical of squamous cell carcinoma than the other options

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: While possible, melanoma is less likely given the lack of specific mention of pigmentation or other characteristic features

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a rare and aggressive cancer, but the description does not specifically suggest its typical features such as rapid growth or neuroendocrine markers

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This is the most common skin cancer but is less likely to metastasize, especially to lymph nodes, as described in this case

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: This is a rare skin cancer that typically grows slowly and is less likely to metastasize to lymph nodes as described
